sources: Isukul, Caroline. 'A Grammar of Agholo [Ogbia]' (draft, Kay Williamson editorial comments)
Lawson-Ikuru, Merosobo. 'The Noun Class System of Ogbia' (JOLAN Supplement Vol. III, 2018)
Evulewuru & Uwasomba. 'Distinctive Study of Izon and Ogbia Grammatical Structures' (EJOSED 2025)
meta.classification: Central Delta language, Cross River family (Niger-Congo). Spoken in Ogbia LGA, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Major varieties: Anyama, Agholo (Kolo group), Otakeme (Oloibiri clan).
meta.word_order: SVO (Subject-Verb-Object) — unlike neighboring Izon (Ijoid family), which is SOV.

alphabet.note_u_and_u_grave: u and u` (a distinct back vowel) never begin a word in Agholo.
alphabet.note_dialectal_variation: The 2018 Otakeme description (Lawson-Ikuru) uses IPA symbols for some of the same sounds: ɔ,ɛ,ə,ɓ,ɗ,ʊ,ɪ where Isukul's Agholo orthography writes ọ,ẹ,ạ(or similar),b`,d`,u,ị. Treat these as orthographic/phonetic variants across sources, not different sounds.
alphabet.vowel_count_note: Sidi Ọlali's 1950s primer proposed 8 vowels; Williamson's 1979 Oloibiri-based orthography (used by Isukul) posits 10 vowel phonemes; Evulewuru & Uwasomba's 2025 comparative paper also counts 10.

vowel_harmony.description: Ogbia/Agholo has near-complete vowel harmony. Vowels split into two harmonizing sets; only vowels from one set normally co-occur within a simple word.
vowel_harmony.spelling_convention: To avoid over-marking, only the FIRST vowel in a word is dotted/marked for the narrow set — later vowels are assumed to harmonize automatically.
vowel_harmony.complex_word_exception: Complex/compound words can mix wide and narrow vowels across their parts; a hyphen marks this compounding (e.g. igbigi-fạri 'file', ạni-óbhom 'woman').

tone_system.description: Ogbia is a tone language. Tone can distinguish otherwise-identical words, and can distinguish nouns from verbs, and statements from questions.

level_tones.downstep: marked with ˥ between syllables (rare, per Lawson-Ikuru: high, low, mid + rare downstep)

gliding_tone.falling: marked with ˆ; restricted to word-final position

tone_system.noun_tone_classes: Disyllabic nouns fall into four tone classes (LL, LH, HH, HL); trisyllabic nouns into six (LLL, LHH, HHH, HLL, LHL, LLH). See Isukul ch.2 for full tables.

noun_morphology.vowel_prefix_rule: Virtually all Ogbia nouns begin with a vowel prefix (e-, ẹ-, a-, ạ-, o-, ọ-, i-, ị-). Consonants do not begin nouns.
noun_morphology.three_back_vowels_never_initial: Per Lawson-Ikuru (Otakeme): the back vowels /u/, /ʊ/ and front vowel /ɪ/ never occur at noun-stem-initial position.

plural_formation_patterns.pattern: invariant singular=plural (many e-, ẹ-, a-, ạ- nouns)
plural_formation_patterns.note: Number then shown only via verb concord/context, or by prefixing ara-/ạra- for emphatic plurality (e.g. araési 'many places', araekpóm 'many baskets').

plural_formation_patterns.pattern: loanwords: a-/ạ- prefixed to English-origin consonant-initial words
plural_formation_patterns.note: same form typically used for singular and plural; ara-/ạra- added if plurality must be stressed

case_marking.object_marker: ma-/mạ- prefixes a noun functioning as a grammatical object; written attached to the noun (it has no independent meaning).

deverbal_nominalisation.infinitive_formation: Prefix a low-toned o-/ọ- to the verb stem (harmonizing vowel choice), e.g. -wura 'wash' → owura 'to wash'.
deverbal_nominalisation.abstract_nouns: Prefix e-, ẹ-, a-, ạ-, or i- to a verb stem for abstract deverbal nouns, e.g. -tete 'fear' → etete 'fear/fright'; -b`igh 'steal' → ab`igh 'theft'.
deverbal_nominalisation.agentives: Prefix o-/ọ- (singular) or i-/ẹ- (plural) to a verb phrase (verb + its object) to form an agent noun, e.g. ọkan ọkan 'to carve carving' → ọkanmaokan 'carver/carpenter', plural ẹkanmaekan.
deverbal_nominalisation.instrumentals: Replace the infinitive prefix with the noun prefix and add suffix -ạma/-oma/-ma/-an, e.g. ọkpabh 'to seize' → ọkpábháma 'scissors'.

determiner.description: The only determiner in Ogbia/Agholo; invariable (doesn't inflect for number); suffixed directly to the noun it modifies.
determiner.cross_check: Lawson-Ikuru (Otakeme) confirms the definite article is a suffix, not a prefix, and that it marks number.

relativisation.marker: -bha suffixed to a verb, meaning 'who' or 'which'
examples: anwúnómbha káóruÕbhá 'the people who didn't come'

noun_class_system_otakeme.source: Lawson-Ikuru 2018; based on the Otakeme variety (Oloibiri clan)
noun_class_system_otakeme.classification_note: Ogbia can be described as having a 'vestigial' noun class system (per Welmers 1973's terms): prefixes alternate for singular/plural with partial semantic correlation and DO show some concordial agreement, but not as robustly as classic Bantu noun classes.

classes.note: invariant singular=plural prefix; number shown via concord only
mixed items whose singular/plural is contextual; also functions as the plural of class 1/3/5

example_full_paradigm_head.attributive: e-mú da-ɓàɪ̀ ni 'a head that is good' / i-mú zɛ-ɓàɪ̀ ni 'heads that are good'
example_full_paradigm_head.predicative: è-mú-ə á-ɓàɪ̀ 'the head is good' / ì-mú-zə̀ wá-ɓàɪ̀ 'the heads are good'
example_full_paradigm_head.demonstrative: e-gú ɔ́-mana 'this door' (parallel pattern, different noun)

pronoun_system.structure: prefix + root; prefix marked [+wide] or [-wide] per vowel harmony
pronoun_system.object_marking: ma-/mạ- prefixes the pronoun when it is a grammatical object

possessive_markers.dependent: d`a- (used attributively before a noun, e.g. 'my house')

pronoun_system.shortened_fast_speech_forms_exist: Full forms (e.g. ótạami 'mine') often contract in fast speech (e.g. ótami).

verb_morphology.root_structure: Every verb has a root/stem; inflectional prefixes and suffixes attach around it. E.g. imperative 'itotóla!' (wash-pl) = i- (plural prefix) + -totól (stem) + -a (extensional suffix).

syllable_types.open_syllable_verbs: All ten vowel phonemes occur root-finally in open-syllable verbs, e.g. orogi 'to abuse' (wide), ọgi 'to go' (narrow).

verb_morphology.infinitive_tone: All infinitives are prefixed with a LOW-toned harmonizing vowel (o- or ọ-); infinitive verbs form a single, uniformly low tone class.
categories: Number concord (verb agrees with subject for singular/plural)
inflectional_devices: number agreement prefixes na- (sg) and wa- (pl)
vowel prefixes i- ị- e- ẹ- o- ọ- a- ạ-
particles ma, mu`, ta, d`ọ, ka
the infix kaka (uncertain status per Isukul's own notes)

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Present Progressive
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: na-/wa- + a-/ạ- prefix on verb stem + high tone throughout
tense_aspect_mood_forms.example: Mí` náárú 'I'm coming' / I`yár wáárú 'We're coming'

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Simple Future
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: same structure as present progressive, but only the LAST vowel of the stem is high-toned

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Perfect
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: same structure again; last stem vowel AND the pronominal subject are low-toned

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Habitual Aspect
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: auxiliary verb ebera + nominalised verb form (prefixed with ma-)
tense_aspect_mood_forms.example: Éki ebera máód`e énám. 'Eki loves eating meat.'

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Immediate Future
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: present-progressive form of oru 'to come' (as auxiliary) + nominalised verb (prefixed ma-)
tense_aspect_mood_forms.example: Mí` naarú máóyel. 'I'm about to go home.'

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Probable Future
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: auxiliary otia ('it's likely') + secondary verb construction
tense_aspect_mood_forms.example: Imád`íó náátia á`lobh. 'The rain is likely to fall.'

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Remote Past
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: impersonal verb naab`orá ('it's been long since...') + relativizer ká + subordinate clause
tense_aspect_mood_forms.example: Naab`orá ká áwa id`é. 'It's been long since they ate.'

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Recent Past
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: prefix kaka ('just') as secondary verb modifier

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Unfulfilled Aspect
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: particle tá- replaces na-/wa- number markers; initial stem vowel becomes i-
tense_aspect_mood_forms.example: Mi táíÕgho.... 'I should have bought but for...'

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Completed Perfect
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: lexical verb ạwéÕlé ('leave') or ạsíÕghé ('finish') placed sentence-finally
tense_aspect_mood_forms.example: Mi náád`e awéÕlé. 'I have finished eating.'

tense_aspect_mood_forms.name: Durative Aspect
tense_aspect_mood_forms.formation: verb reduplication to emphasize prolonged activity (Isukul flags this analysis as tentative)
tense_aspect_mood_forms.example: Nwá náása asâ? 'You're engaged in cooking?'

monosyllabic_closed_syllable.singular: no prefix; high tone; suffix -E (copies stem's high tone)
monosyllabic_closed_syllable.plural: low-toned i- prefix; first syllable stays high, final syllable becomes low

monosyllabic_open_syllable_high_vowels.description: verbs ending in high front/back vowels -i/-u take suffix -E in both sg and pl

imperative.polysyllabic: high and low tone occur in free variation in the singular imperative (e.g. otibira → tíbírá or tibira, both meaning 'turn!')
imperative.inceptive_imperative: Composed of imperative form of orere ('to go') or ọkom ('to start') + present progressive of the main verb, e.g. Reré náárú! 'Start coming!'
imperative.hortative: Made with olei ('to reach') in primary construction + infinitive verb preceded by particle ma, e.g. NaáÕléí má`ógi. 'It's time to go./Let's go!'

prefixes: ta- (used with hortative negation and modal 'could have')
negation.hortative_negation: requires BOTH prefix ta- AND suffix -d`ọ, e.g. TaóléiÕd`ọ máód`e 'Let's not eat!'

syntax.basic_word_order: SVO (Subject-Verb-Object), matching English and unlike Izon (SOV). Confirmed independently by Evulewuru & Uwasomba (2025) with the example: Ani-BhoGi-Me-Ewel (S-V-O) 'the man killed the goat'.
syntax.serial_verb_constructions: Prepositional notions are frequently expressed by stringing two verbs together rather than using a preposition, e.g. oghil ó`d`ua (run + go-out) = 'to run away'; omen ód`igh (fall + enter) = 'to fall into'.
syntax.homophonous_grammatical_morphemes: Ogbia has many grammatical morphemes that are spelled/pronounced alike but serve different functions depending on context — most notably -ma- (preposition 'in/at/on/from/towards' when written separately, vs. agentive/complement marker when written attached) and -ka- (question particle / intensifier / conjunction / negative imperative prefix).

izon_ogbia_contrast.language_families: Izon = Ijoid family; Ogbia = Cross River family (both are 'Ijaw'/Niger Delta ethnically, but genetically distinct language families)
izon_ogbia_contrast.consonant_cluster_handling: Neither language tolerates English-style consonant clusters; both insert vowels to break them up when borrowing English words (e.g. English 'school' → Izon 'sukulu', Ogbia 'isukulu'; English 'driver' → Izon 'deraiva', Ogbia 'idrava').
izon_ogbia_contrast.vowel_initial_tendency: Ogbia nouns overwhelmingly begin with vowels; when borrowing English words, Ogbia speakers tend to impose a vowel prefix on the loanword (isukulu, ibasikoro, idrava, imagoro) more consistently than Izon speakers do.
izon_ogbia_contrast.mutual_intelligibility: The study found NO mutual intelligibility between Izon and Ogbia, despite both being spoken in Bayelsa State and both being considered part of the broader 'Ijaw' ethnic/cultural grouping.
izon_ogbia_contrast.shared_cognates_with_efik: Ogbia and Efik (also Cross River family) share a number of cognates, e.g. 'ten': Efik diop / Ogbia diobh; 'not': Efik ba / Ogbia ba; 'until': Efik tutu / Ogbia tutu.

word_division_rules.hyphen_use: Introduced to write complex/compound words that mix vowels from the wide and narrow harmony sets (see vowel_harmony above).
